complete deterministic batch execution plus the final incremental V1.41 test.

## 22. Next step — V1.42 micro-scope

V1.41 closes the same-key concurrent-build question. The next step should not add another
cache mechanism. It should audit the **real consumer/lifetime boundary** that still does
not exist in production:

1. search for the first real production caller that could own a `ResolutionCache`;
2. if none exists, keep the cache explicitly caller-owned and do not invent a renderer/global owner;
3. inspect renderer/frame/scene orchestration for a natural cache hand-off point;
4. if a real consumer exists, test cache lifetime across actual frame boundaries rather than simulated ones;
5. measure cache capacity against real scene/component cardinality, not synthetic 1/10/100/1000 alone;
6. measure retained memory with the real production object graph and allocator behavior if a consumer exists;
7. compare cache reuse against graph rebuild frequency and dependency churn;
8. determine whether cache partitioning by scene/frame would reduce LRU pollution;
9. test teardown semantics so discarded scenes cannot retain live component graphs through cached results;
10. revisit serialized fingerprint envelopes only if a real persistence/restart requirement appears;
11. keep `ResolutionFingerprint.cache_identity` as the only dependency identity;
12. repeat cross-surface invalidation and concurrent tests after any lifetime change;
13. preserve the COLOR boundary strictly.

The gate for V1.42 should be **evidence of a real production lifetime**, not an invented
cache manager.
